papers.title: A Methylcellulose Hydrogel as Support for 3D Plotting of Complex Shaped Calcium Phosphate Scaffolds.
papers.abstract: 3D plotting is an additive manufacturing technology enabling biofabrication, thus the integration of cells or biologically sensitive proteins or growth factors into the manufacturing process. However, most (bio-)inks developed for 3D plotting were not shown to be processed into clinically relevant geometries comprising critical overhangs and cavities, which would collapse without a sufficient support material. Herein, we have developed a support hydrogel ink based on methylcellulose (mc), which is able to act as support as long as the co-plotted main structure is not stable. Therefore, 6 w/v %, 8 w/v % and 10 w/v % mc were allowed to swell in water, resulting in viscous inks, which were characterized for their rheological and extrusion properties. The successful usage of 10 w/v % mc as support ink was proven by multichannel plotting of the support together with a plottable calcium phosphate cement (CPC) acting as main structure. CPC scaffolds displaying critical overhangs or a large central cavity could be plotted accurately with the newly developed mc support ink. The dissolution properties of mc allowed complete removal of the gel without residuals, once CPC setting was finished. Finally, we fabricated a scaphoid bone model by computed tomography data acquisition and co-extrusion of CPC and the mc support hydrogel.

llm.relevance_to_user: 这篇论文不涉及任何人工智能方法或机器学习模型，与AI生物打印研究方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not embed AI into any bioprinting workflow stage; it focuses on material development for support hydrogels with no computational modeling or automation.

summary_zh.motivation: 开发一种支撑水凝胶墨水，用于制造具有复杂几何形状的骨组织工程支架。
summary_zh.method: 制备不同浓度的甲基纤维素水凝胶，并对其流变性和挤出性能进行表征，与磷酸钙水泥共挤出。
summary_zh.result: 10%甲基纤维素墨水能成功支撑具有临界悬垂和大空腔的支架，并在水泥固化后完全溶解去除。
summary_zh.validation: 通过流变测试和共挤出实验验证支撑墨水的可行性。

summary_en.motivation: To develop a support hydrogel ink enabling the fabrication of complex geometries in 3D plotting of calcium phosphate scaffolds.
summary_en.method: Methylcellulose hydrogels of varying concentrations were characterized rheologically and co-extruded with calcium phosphate cement to form scaffolds with overhangs and cavities.
summary_en.result: The 10% methylcellulose ink effectively supported the main structure and could be completely removed after cement setting.
summary_en.validation: Rheological characterization and successful printing of complex geometries including a scaphoid bone model.
